name: manual_cc2a07
claim: Pre-push hooks rejecting rewritten history (e.g. after git filter-repo) means author identities changed and no longer match the allowlist — the fix is to repair the rewritten identities (correct .mailmap or re-author the affected commits) and re-run the repository's hygiene checks under scripts/git/, not to bypass the hook. If an exceptional bypass is ever genuinely warranted, it requires explicit human approval beforehand and immediate post-push verification (re-run the hygiene check against the pushed ref) — never a default remediation. The --force-with-lease=<branch>:<old-sha> pattern remains mandatory for any force-push: it records the expected remote SHA and refuses if someone else pushed in the meantime.

decisions.notes: Replaces --no-verify remediation guidance with repair-and-reverify guidance, per CodeRabbit review finding on PR #256's related lessons audit. Preserves the correct --force-with-lease safety pattern.
